evidence.note: Explicit stated intent to build monolithically: 'I'll write a comprehensive zstd_decompress.c implementing the full RFC 8878 spec... I'll write it all into a single file.' No milestone breakdown with done-conditions; the plan is one undifferentiated push.

The code was written in chunks (EOF_PART1..11) that DO follow a sensible dependency order — bitstreams → FSE → Huffman → literals → sequences → blocks → frame header → dictionary → main entry. This is genuine dependency-aware sequencing of components, above pure 'vague ordering', but each chunk's milestone is essentially 'write more code'.

First compile and first test.sh run only AFTER the entire decoder was written. Nothing was verifiable until everything was done — the exact monolithic-push antipattern; no per-subsystem landing checkpoint or smallest-possible test input per component.

The agent only discovered which subsystems worked in isolation reactively during debugging (img.png = raw block, repetitive = predef FSE, simple = raw) rather than having designed a walking-skeleton path that verified each layer as a milestone. No deliberate re-ordering when dependencies surfaced.

Entire back half is undifferentiated debugging of one entangled build; because HUF/FSE/sequences were all landed together, a single Huffman-weight bug left three of six inputs failing with no isolated checkpoint to localize which subsystem was proven-good.

reasoning: The agent showed a real, dependency-respecting order in the sequence of code chunks it wrote (FSE before Huffman before sequences before dictionaries), which lifts it above anchor 3's 'vague ordering in the head.' But it explicitly chose to write the whole decoder before any compile or test, so components were fully entangled, nothing was verifiable until everything was done, and its milestones were literally 'write the next chunk' — matching anchor 3's core failure mode. It never landed-and-verified a subsystem before moving on, never picked a walking-skeleton path, and gave no subsystem its own done-signal (anchor 5+). Interpolating between the genuine dependency ordering and the monolithic, checkpoint-free execution places it at 4.
